title: 4–5. Perfection and beatitude when the end is attained; the highest good defined as last and most perfect
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss: and most perfect, because it excludes every defect plus need, plus gives itself to the one who has it so that same it may be perfectly well with him. because it stands as subjected to no other as a means, or stands as not at all ordered to the attaining belonging toward something higher plus greater; — the highest good stands as called also the last. 5. wretched, plus unhappy if it falls from plus stands as deprived belonging toward its end plus good — but on the contrary it stands as imperfect. plus it does not fall to things without reason to be blessed, as Augustine teaches in the book belonging toward eighty-three questions, question 1; — for no animal that same lacks knowledge can be blessed. Each thing, if it attains its good plus end, stands as perfect — or, if its nature stands as intelligent, blessed. 4.
pass_b_english: 4. Each thing, if it attains its good and end, is perfect — or, if its nature is intelligent, blessed. For no animal that lacks knowledge can be blessed, and it does not fall to things without reason to be blessed, as Augustine teaches in the book of eighty-three questions, question 1; but on the contrary it is imperfect, wretched, and unhappy if it falls from and is deprived of its end and good.

5. The highest good is called also the last, because it is subjected to no other as a means, or is not at all ordered to the attaining of something higher and greater; and most perfect, because it excludes every defect and need, and gives itself to the one who has it so that it may be perfectly well with him.
source_text: 4. Una quaeque res, si bonum, finemque suum assequatur, perfecta est, sive, si natura sit intelligens, beata. Nam nullum animal, quod scientia caret, beatum esse potest, & non cadit in rationis expertia, ut beata sint, docente Augustino lib. 83 quaestionum, quaest. 1, contra vero imperfecta, misera & infelix est, si fine & bono suo excidat ac privetur. 5. Summum bonum dicitur & ultimum, quia nulli alteri, tanquam medium, subjicitur, seu ad aliud superius & majus consequendum minime ordinatur: perfectissimum, quia omnem defectum & indigentiam excludit, & habenti sese dat, ut ei perfecte bene sit.
